newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's PUMA issuing A$500 mln of bonds.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's PUMA issuing A$500 mln of bonds.

text.p: Macquarie Bank said on Wednesday its securitisation division PUMA Management Ltd is issuing A$500 million of bonds into the domestic market today.
It added that the issue is part of a total A$3.0 billion funding expected over calendar 1997.
PUMA Managing director Tony Gill said the bonds are launched from its Masterfund P6 and would be known as P-6 Series A. Pricing would be on February 13 and settled on February 18.
There are four tranches in the issue, with one fixed rate and the remaining three in floating rate structures.
Tranches one, two and three are rated AAA/Aaa by Standard & Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service.
Tranche four, which is subordinated debt, is rated AA minus by S&P.

Gill said Tranche 1-F would be a fixed rate with a face value of A$315 million and maturing April 15, 2000. Pricing would be at a margin over the benchmark Commonwealth Government 7.0 percent April 2000 bond.

Of the floating tranches, Tranche 2 would have a face value of A$135 million and an average expected life of 7.1 years, while Tranches 3 and 4 would have a face value of A$25 million each and have average expected lives of 7.6 years.
This is PUMA's first issue of 1997 and part of a A$3.0 billion total funding programme for the year, a percentage of which was expected to be raised offshore.
A large portion of these funds would go to Aussie Home Loans, one of Australia's leading non-bank home loan lenders.
PUMA raised A$1.3 billion in the domestic market during calender year 1996.
